SNAP Restaurant Meals Program: Which States Accept EBT

Updated November 3, 2026Source: USDA SNAP Retailer Locator & FNA
Short answer: The Restaurant Meals Program (RMP) is a state option within SNAP that lets certain eligible recipients use their EBT card to buy hot, prepared meals at approved restaurants — something regular SNAP does not allow. It runs in about 10 states, led by California and Arizona. It is not open to every SNAP recipient: generally you must be 60 or older, have a disability, or be experiencing homelessness (plus your spouse). If you qualify and live in a participating state, you can use EBT at fast food and sit-down restaurants that display RMP approval.

Most people are told SNAP can't buy hot or prepared food — and for the vast majority, that's true. The Restaurant Meals Program is the exception, and it's one of the least-understood parts of SNAP. Here's exactly how it works.

What RMP actually is

RMP is a state option: each state decides whether to run it. Where it exists, specific restaurants sign up and get authorized to accept EBT from eligible recipients. Regular SNAP blocks hot and restaurant food; RMP carves out an exception for people who often can't cook or store groceries.

Which states have the Restaurant Meals Program

Based on the USDA's current list of authorized restaurants, RMP operates in these states (California and Arizona have by far the most locations):

  • California — the largest RMP by far, statewide
  • Arizona — statewide
  • New York
  • Michigan
  • Virginia
  • Illinois
  • Maryland
  • Rhode Island
  • Massachusetts
  • New Jersey (limited)

If your state isn't on this list, EBT can't be used at restaurants there — you can still use it for groceries and cold prepared items under normal SNAP rules. States join and expand RMP over time, so it's worth rechecking. Browse participating states to see cities and restaurants.

RMP vs regular SNAP, side by side

Regular SNAPRMP
Hot/prepared foodNot allowedAllowed at approved restaurants
Who can use itAll SNAP recipientsEligible recipients only (60+, disabled, homeless)
WhereGrocery/retail storesAuthorized restaurants in participating states
What you buyGroceries to prepareReady-to-eat meals

Why the program exists

People who are older, have a disability, or are experiencing homelessness often lack a kitchen, storage, or the ability to cook. RMP means their benefits still translate into actual meals. That's also why eligibility is limited — it targets those specific situations, not SNAP recipients in general. See who qualifies.

Frequently asked questions

Can any SNAP recipient use EBT at restaurants?

No. Even in participating states, only recipients who are 60 or older, have a disability, or are experiencing homelessness (and their spouses) are enrolled in RMP. Everyone else follows normal SNAP rules — no hot or restaurant food.

Which state has the most RMP restaurants?

California, by a wide margin, followed by Arizona. Between them they hold the large majority of authorized RMP restaurants nationwide.

Does my regular EBT card work at McDonald's?

Only if you're enrolled in RMP in a participating state and that McDonald's is authorized. A standard SNAP case in a non-RMP state cannot buy restaurant food.
